And know that when He, exalted is He, said, "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared" [al-Isra': 57], He explained that every town, together with its people, must have its condition return to one of two matters: either destruction (al-ihlak) or punishment (al-ta'dhib). Muqatil said: "As for the righteous town, it is by death; as for the wicked town, it is by punishment." It was also said that what is meant by His words, "And there is not a town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment," is the towns of the disbelievers. Their end must be one of two matters: either complete eradication (al-istí'sal), which is what is meant by destruction, or a punishment severe but short of that, such as the killing of their chieftains and the Muslims' domination over them through taking captives (al-saby), seizing wealth (ightinam al-amwal), and imposing the jizya (poll tax). Then He, exalted is He, explained that this ruling is a decisive and certain ruling, so He said: "That was written in the Book as a decree (mastura)." Its meaning is clear.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a warning﴾ [al-Isra': 59]. And: ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people. And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [as for] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We warn them, but it increases them in nothing but great transgression."﴾ [al-Isra': 60].

Page 187

He, exalted is He, when He mentioned the proof against the invalidity of the polytheists' statement and followed it with the threat, followed it with the mention of the matter of prophethood. That is because the Quraysh disbelievers demanded from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the manifestation of great, overpowering miracles, as Allah related about them that they said: ﴿Let him bring us a sign as the former messengers were sent﴾ [al-Anbiya': 5]. Others said that what is meant is what they asked for when they said: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring"﴾ [al-Isra': 90]. It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the people said: "You claim that before you there were prophets, among them one for whom the wind was subjected, and among them one who used to revive the dead. So bring us something of these miracles." Allah, exalted is He, answered this doubt with His words: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them.﴾ There are several interpretations of this answer:

The first aspect: the meaning is that if He, exalted is He, had manifested those overpowering miracles and then they did not believe in them, but remained persistent in their disbelief, then they would deserve the punishment of extermination. But sending the punishment of extermination upon this nation is not permissible, because Allah, exalted is He, knows that among them there are those who will believe or whose descendants will believe. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, did not grant them their request and did not manifest those overpowering miracles. Ibn 'Abbas related that "the people of Makkah asked the Messenger ﷺ to turn Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains so that they might cultivate those lands. The Messenger ﷺ asked Allah for that, and Allah, exalted is He, said: 'If you wish, I will do that, but on condition that if they disbelieve, I will destroy them.' The Messenger ﷺ said: '"I do not want that; rather, bear with them patiently."' Then this verse was revealed."

The second aspect: in explaining this answer, we do not manifest these miracles because your fathers who saw them did not believe in them, and you are imitators of them. So if you saw them yourselves, you would not believe in them either.

The third aspect: the former peoples witnessed these miracles and denied them. Allah knew about you as well that if you witnessed them, you would deny them. So their manifestation would be pointless, and the Wise does not do what is pointless.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her﴾, and concerning it there are discussions:

The first discussion: the meaning is that the sign they sought is like the sign of Thamud. We gave Thamud [the sign] clear and evident, then they disbelieved in it, and so they deserved the punishment of extermination. How then would these people desire it by way of demand and arbitrary dictation against Allah, exalted is He?

The second discussion: His words, "visible" (mubsira). In it there are two aspects:
The first: al-Farra' said: "mubsira" means "illuminating" (mudi'a), as He said: ﴿And the day as a visible one﴾ [Yunus: 67], meaning illuminating.
The second: "mubsira" means "having sight," i.e., in it is sight: whoever contemplates it sees by it his right guidance and derives evidence from it for the truthfulness of that Messenger.

The third discussion: His words, "but they wronged her," meaning they wronged themselves by denying it. Ibn Qutaybah said: "They wronged her" means they denied that it was from Allah, exalted is He.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We send not the signs except as a warning﴾. It was said: there is no sign except that it includes a warning in case of denial, either of the hastened punishment or of the punishment of the Hereafter.

If it is said: the greatest purpose in manifesting signs is that they be used as evidence for the truthfulness of the claimant; how then does He limit the purpose of their manifestation to warning?

We say: The purpose is that when a claimant to prophethood manifests a sign, the people hear that he has manifested a sign, but they do not know whether that sign is a miracle or a warning. They only consider it possible that it is a miracle. And supposing it is a miracle, if they do not reflect upon it and do not derive evidence from it for truthfulness, they deserve severe punishment. This is the fear which moves them to reflect and contemplate those miracles. So what is meant by His words, "And We send not the signs except as a warning," is this which we have mentioned. And Allah knows best.

Know that when the people demanded overpowering miracles from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, exalted is He, answered that manifesting them was not in their interest, this became a cause for the boldness of those disbelievers to attack him and to say to him: "If you were truly a messenger from Allah, exalted is He, you would have brought us these miracles which we have proposed to you, just as Moses and the other prophets brought them." At this, Allah strengthened his heart and made clear to him that He, exalted is He, would support and aid him. So He said: ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people."﴾ In it there are two views:

The first view: the meaning is that His wisdom and His power encompass the people, so they are in His grip and power. When this is so, they cannot do anything except by His decree and destiny. The intended meaning is as if He, exalted is He, says to him: "We will support you and strengthen you until you convey Our message and make Our religion manifest." Al-Hasan said: "He prevented them from killing him, as He said: ﴿And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67]."

The second view: the people meant by "the people" are the people of Makkah, and Allah's encompassing them means that He will open it (Makkah) to the believers. So the meaning is: "And when We gave you good news that Allah has encompassed the people of Makkah," meaning that He will overpower them, subdue them, and make your dominion over them manifest. A parallel to this is His words: ﴿The multitude will be defeated and will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45], and His words: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 12]. And His words, "has encompassed the people": since everything Allah reports will occur is necessarily to occur, from this standpoint it is as if it had already occurred, and therefore He said: "has encompassed the people." It is related that "when the two armies drew near one another on the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in the tent with Abu Bakr, and he was supplicating and saying: 'O Allah, I ask You for Your covenant and Your promise to me.' Then he went out, wearing his armor, urging the people on and saying: ﴿The multitude will be defeated and will turn their backs﴾ [al-Qamar: 45]."

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. Concerning this "sight" there are several sayings:

The first saying: Allah showed Muhammad in a dream the places of death (masari') of the Quraysh disbelievers. When he arrived at the water of Badr, he said: "By Allah, it is as if I am looking at the places where the people will fall," and then he began to say: "This is the place where so-and-so will fall, this is the place where so-and-so will fall." When the Quraysh heard that, they made his vision an object of mockery, and they used to hasten what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had been promised.

The second saying: what is meant is his vision in which he saw that he would enter Makkah, and he informed his companions of that. When he was prevented from the Sacred House in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah, that became a trial for some of the people. 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: "Did not the Messenger of Allah ﷺ inform us that we would enter the House and circumambulate it?" Abu Bakr said: "He did not inform us that we would do that this year; so we will do it in another year." When the following year came, he entered it, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Certainly did Allah fulfill for His Messenger the vision in truth﴾ [al-Fath: 27]. They objected to these two sayings, saying: "This surah is Meccan, and these two events are Medinan." This objection is weak, because these two events were in Medina, but their being seen in a dream is not far-fetched to have occurred in Makkah.

The third saying: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw the Banu Umayyah climbing upon his minbar like monkeys, and that displeased him." This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas in the narration of 'Ata'. The objection mentioned applies to it as well, because this verse is Meccan, and there was no minbar for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Makkah. It may be answered that it is not far-fetched that in Makkah he saw that he had a minbar in Medina which the Banu Umayyah would take turns occupying.

The fourth saying, which is the most correct and is the saying of most exegetes: what is meant by it is what Allah showed him on the night of the Isra' (Night Journey). They differed about the meaning of this vision. Most said: there is no difference between "ru'yah" (sight) and "ru'ya" (vision) in the language; one says "ra'aytu bi-'aynī ru'yatan wa ru'yā" (I saw with my eye, a seeing and a vision). The minority said: this indicates that the story of the Isra' took place only in a dream, but this view is weak and false according to what we established at the beginning of this surah. His words, "except as a trial for the people," mean: when the Prayer and Peace be upon him mentioned to them the story of the Isra', they denied him, and many who had believed in him disbelieved in him, while the sincere ones increased in faith. For this reason it was a test.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the accursed tree in the Qur'an﴾. This is by way of inversion, and the sense is: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you and the accursed tree in the Qur'an except as a trial for the people." It was also said that the meaning is: "And the accursed tree in the Qur'an is likewise." They differed about this tree. Most said: it is the tree of Zaqqum mentioned in the Qur'an in His words: ﴿Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum, food of the sinful﴾ [al-Dukhan: 43-44]. This trial in mentioning this tree was in two respects:

The first: Abu Jahl said: "Your companion claims that the fire of Hell burns stones, since he said: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24]. Then he says that in the fire there is a tree, and the fire consumes trees, so how can trees grow in it?"

The second: Ibn al-Zib'ara said: "We know zaqqum only as dates and butter, so eat of it." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed, when they were amazed that there should be a tree in the fire: ﴿Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Saffat: 63], and the verses.

If it is said: there is no cursing of this tree in the Qur'an.
We say: there are several aspects to this:
The first: what is meant is cursing the disbelievers who eat it.
The second: the Arabs say of every disagreeable, harmful food that it is accursed.
The third: cursing in the original language means distancing; since this accursed tree in the Qur'an is distanced from all qualities of good, it was called accursed.

The second saying: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "The tree is the Banu Umayyah, meaning al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As." He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw in a dream that the sons of Marwan were taking turns on his minbar, so he related his vision to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, while he was alone in his house with them. When they dispersed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard al-Hakam reporting the Messenger of Allah's vision. This grieved him greatly, and he suspected 'Umar of divulging his secret. Then it became clear that al-Hakam had been eavesdropping on them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ banished him."

Al-Wahidi said: this story took place in Medina, and the surah is Meccan, so this interpretation is far-fetched, unless it is said that this verse is Medinan, but no one has said that. What confirms this interpretation is the saying of 'A'ishah to Marwan: "May Allah curse your father, and you were in his loins; so you are among those whom Allah has cursed."

The third opinion: the accursed tree in the Qur'an is the Jews, based on His saying, ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78].

If someone says: when the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring compelling miracles, he replied that there was no benefit in showing them, because if they appeared and you did not believe, Allah would send down upon you the punishment of annihilation, and that is not permissible. What connection does this speech have to the mention of the vision that became a trial for people, and to the mention of the tree that became a trial for people?

We say: The sense is as if it were said: when they asked for these miracles, and then you did not show them, their non-appearance became a doubt for them about whether you were truthful in your claim to prophethood. However, the occurrence of this doubt does not weaken your affair, nor does it become a cause of weakness in your condition. The second saying: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "The tree is the Banu Umayyah, meaning al-Hakam ibn Abi al-'As." He said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw in a dream that the sons of Marwan were taking turns on his minbar, so he related his vision to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, while he was alone in his house with them. When they dispersed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard al-Hakam reporting the Messenger of Allah's vision. This grieved him greatly, and he suspected 'Umar of divulging his secret. Then it became clear that al-Hakam had been eavesdropping on them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ banished him."

Al-Wahidi said: this story took place in Medina, and the surah is Meccan, so this interpretation is far-fetched, unless it is said that this verse is Medinan, but no one has said that. What confirms this interpretation is the saying of 'A'ishah to Marwan: "May Allah curse your father, and you were in his loins; so you are among those whom Allah has cursed."

The third opinion: the accursed tree in the Qur'an is the Jews, based on His saying, ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 78].

If someone says: when the people asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to bring compelling miracles, he replied that there was no benefit in showing them, because if they appeared and you did not believe, Allah would send down upon you the punishment of annihilation, and that is not permissible. What connection does this speech have to the mention of the vision that became a trial for people, and to the mention of the tree that became a trial for people?

We say: The sense is as if it were said: when they asked for these miracles, and then you did not show them, their non-appearance became a doubt for them about whether you were truthful in your claim to prophethood. However, the occurrence of this doubt does not weaken your affair, nor does it become a cause of weakness in your condition. Do you not see that the mention of that vision became a cause for a great doubt to arise in hearts? Yet the strength of those doubts did not cause weakness in your affair, nor slackness in the unity of those who are sincere toward you. Likewise, this doubt arising from the non-appearance of these miracles does not necessitate slackness in your condition, nor weakness in your affair. And Allah knows best.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾. The purpose of this is to mention another reason why He did not manifest the miracles they proposed. These people were warned with the fears of this world and the Hereafter, and with the tree of Zaqqum, yet this warning only increased them in great transgression. That indicates the hardness of their hearts and their persistence in error and rebellion. Since the matter is so, even if Allah were to show them those miracles they proposed, they would not benefit from them, and they would only increase in persistence in ignorance and obstinacy. And when that is the case, wisdom requires that Allah not show them the signs and miracles they proposed. And Allah knows best.

And know that when He, exalted is He, said, "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared" [al-Isra': 57], He explained that every town, together with its people, must have its condition return to one of two matters: either destruction (al-ihlak) or punishment (al-ta'dhib). Muqatil said: "As for the righteous town, it is by death; as for the wicked town, it is by punishment." It was also said that what is meant by His words, "And there is not a town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment," is the towns of the disbelievers. Their end must be one of two matters: either complete eradication (al-istí'sal), which is what is meant by destruction, or a punishment severe but short of that, such as the killing of their chieftains and the Muslims' domination over them through taking captives (al-saby), seizing wealth (ightinam al-amwal), and imposing the jizya (poll tax). Then He, exalted is He, explained that this ruling is a decisive and certain ruling, so He said: "That was written in the Book as a decree (mastura)." Its meaning is clear.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a warning﴾ [al-Isra': 59]. And: ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people. And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [as for] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. He, exalted is He, when He mentioned the proof against the invalidity of the polytheists' statement and followed it with the threat, followed it with the mention of the matter of prophethood. That is because the Quraysh disbelievers demanded from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the manifestation of great, overpowering miracles, as Allah related about them that they said: ﴿Let him bring us a sign as the former messengers were sent﴾ [al-Anbiya': 5]. Others said that what is meant is what they asked for when they said: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring"﴾ [al-Isra': 90]. It is related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that the people said: "You claim that before you there were prophets, among them one for whom the wind was subjected, and among them one who used to revive the dead. Allah, exalted is He, answered this doubt with His words: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them.﴾ There are several interpretations of this answer:

The first aspect: the meaning is that if He, exalted is He, had manifested those overpowering miracles and then they did not believe in them, but remained persistent in their disbelief, then they would deserve the punishment of extermination. But sending the punishment of extermination upon this nation is not permissible, because Allah, exalted is He, knows that among them there are those who will believe or whose descendants will believe. For this reason, Allah, exalted is He, did not grant them their request and did not manifest those overpowering miracles. Ibn 'Abbas related that "the people of Makkah asked the Messenger ﷺ to turn Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains so that they might cultivate those lands. The Messenger ﷺ asked Allah for that, and Allah, exalted is He, said: 'If you wish, I will do that, but on condition that if they disbelieve, I will destroy them.' The Messenger ﷺ said: '"I do not want that; rather, bear with them patiently."' Then this verse was revealed."

The second aspect: in explaining this answer, we do not manifest these miracles because your fathers who saw them did not believe in them, and you are imitators of them. So if you saw them yourselves, you would not believe in them either.

The third aspect: the former peoples witnessed these miracles and denied them. Allah knew about you as well that if you witnessed them, you would deny them. So their manifestation would be pointless, and the Wise does not do what is pointless.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 17, verses 62–63:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Tell me, is this the one You have honored over me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few."﴾ ﴿He said, "Go! Whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense."﴾ In this passage there are several issues.

The first issue: concerning the manner of the coherence (*nazm*, the arrangement and connection of the verses), there are several aspects.

The first: Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in a great trial from his people and the people of his time, He explained that the condition of the prophets with the people of their times was similar. Do you not see that the first of the friends of Allah was Adam, and then he was in a severe trial from Iblis?

The second: the people only disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), opposed him, and proposed to him false suggestions, for two reasons: arrogance and envy. As for arrogance, their pride prevented them from submitting. As for envy, they envied him for what Allah had given him of prophethood and high rank. So He, exalted is He, explained that these two, arrogance and envy, are what led Iblis to leave faith and enter disbelief. Thus this is an ancient affliction and a great trial for creation.

The third: when He, exalted is He, described them by saying ﴿But it only increases them in great rebellion﴾ [al-Isra: 60], He explained what is the cause of the occurrence of this rebellion, namely the saying of Iblis, ﴿I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few.﴾ For the sake of this purpose, Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the story of Iblis and Adam. This is the discussion concerning the manner of the coherence.

The second issue: know that Allah, exalted is He, has mentioned this story in seven surahs: al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr, this surah, al-Kahf, Ta-Ha, and Sad. The complete discussion of it has already been given in al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, and al-Hijr, so there is no benefit in repetition, but there is no harm in enumerating some issues:

The first issue: they differed as to whether those commanded to prostrate to Adam were all the angels or specifically the angels of the earth. The apparent wording "the angels" indicates generality, but His saying, exalted is He, at the end of surah al-A'raf, describing the angels of the heavens, ﴿and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206], requires that the angels of the heavens be excluded from this generality.

The second issue: the prostration in this context may mean placing the forehead on the ground, or it may mean a greeting. On the first interpretation, was Adam the one prostrated to, or is it said that the one prostrated to was Allah, exalted is He, and Adam was a direction (*qiblah*) for the prostration?

The third issue: is Iblis among the angels or not? If he was not among the angels, how does the command to the angels to prostrate include him?

The fourth issue: was Iblis a disbeliever from the very beginning, or is it said that he only disbelieved at that time?

The fifth issue: did the angels prostrate to Adam from the moment his life was complete, or after that?

The sixth issue: is Iblis's argument for refusing to prostrate his saying ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾, or something else?

The seventh issue: these verses indicate that Iblis knew his Lord, but he fell into disbelief because of arrogance and envy. Some have denied this and said he never knew Allah at all.

The eighth issue: what is the wisdom behind Allah granting Iblis respite and giving him power over creation to whisper (*waswasah*)?

Let us return to the exegesis. We say: in this verse, He, exalted is He, related from Iblis one kind of action and two kinds of speech. As for the action, it is that he did not prostrate to Adam, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿they prostrated, except Iblis﴾. As for the two kinds of speech:

The first of them is his saying ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ This is an interrogative with the meaning of denial. Its meaning is that my origin is more noble than his origin, so it is necessary that I be more noble than him, and it is repugnant to reason that the more noble be commanded to serve the less noble.

The second kind of his speech is his saying ﴿Tell me, is this the one You have honored over me?﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: His saying ﴿Tell me (*ara'aytaka*)﴾ means "inform me." We have already investigated this expression in the commentary on surah al-An'am. His saying ﴿is this the one You have honored over me﴾ has several aspects:

The first: its meaning is "Inform me about this one whom You have preferred over me. Why did You prefer him over me, when I am better than him?" Then the speech was shortened because it is understood.

The second: it may be said that this is a subject with the interrogative particle omitted, and "the one" with its relative clause is the predicate. Its estimated form is "Inform me, is this the one whom You have honored over me!" This is in a manner of belittling and disparaging. The interrogative particle was omitted because its presence in His saying ﴿ara'aytaka﴾ made its repetition unnecessary.

The third aspect: this may be the object of "ara'ayta," because the *kaf* came merely for the address and has no grammatical position. It is as if he said, in a manner of wonder and denial, "Did you see or know this one whom you have honored over me?", meaning: if you had seen him or known him, you would have been obligated not to honor him over me. This is the real meaning of this expression. Then Allah, exalted is He, said, relating [from him], ﴿If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few.﴾ Concerning this there are discussions:

The first discussion: Ibn Kathir read ﴿akhkhartani﴾ with the *ya'* (the final "ya" of the first person) retained both in pausing and in continuous recitation. 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read it with the *ya'* omitted. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr retained it in continuous recitation but omitted it in pausing.

The second discussion: concerning *ihtinak* there are two views:

One of them: it is an expression for taking entirely. It is said: "Fulan *ihtanaka* what Fulan has of wealth," when he exhausted it and took it entirely. And "the locusts *ihtanaka* the crop" when they consumed it entirely.

The second: it comes from the Arab saying "*hannaka* the animal, *yuhannikuha*," when one places a rope under its lower jaw by which he leads it. Abu Muslim said: *ihtinak* is a form from *hanak* (the jaw/palate), as if they [the descendants] are controlled by him as the rider controls his horse by its bridle. According to the first view, the meaning of the verse is "I will certainly uproot them through misguidance." According to the second view, the meaning is "I will certainly lead them to sins as the animal is led by its rope."

The third discussion: His saying ﴿except a few﴾ refers to those whom Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. If it is asked: how did Iblis form this true assumption concerning the descendants of Adam? We say: there are several aspects:

The first: he heard the angels saying ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], so he came to know these conditions.

The second: he whispered to Adam and did not find in him determination, so he assumed that his offspring would be like him in weakness of resolve.

The third: he knew that man is composed of a bestial appetitive power, a predatory irascible power, an imaginative satanic power, and a rational angelic power. He knew that the three powers, namely the appetitive, the irascible, and the imaginative, are the ones that dominate at the beginning of creation, and that the rational power is only perfected at the end. When the matter is like this, what Iblis said is necessarily true.

Know that when He, exalted is He, related this from Iblis, He related from Himself that He said to him, "Go." This "go" is not the going which is the opposite of coming; rather its meaning is "proceed to your affair which you have chosen," and the intent is to leave him free and to entrust the matter to him.

Then He said ﴿Whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense.﴾ A parallel to this is the saying of Musa, peace be upon him, ﴿So go, for you will have in this life that you say, "No touching"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 97]. If it is asked: is it not better to say "indeed Hell is their recompense, a full recompense," so that this pronoun refers back to His saying ﴿whoever follows you﴾? We say there are several aspects:

The first: the estimated form is "indeed Hell is their recompense and your recompense," then the addressee was given precedence over the absent party, so it was said "your recompense."

The second: it is permissible that this address is directed to the absent parties by way of *iltifat* (the shift from one grammatical person to another).

The third: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: ("Whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection.") So every act of disobedience that occurs results in Iblis acquiring a share equal to the burden of that doer. Since Iblis is the origin of all acts of disobedience, the one addressed with the threat is Iblis. Then He said ﴿a full recompense (*jaza'an mawfuran*)﴾. This word may be used transitively and intransitively. As for the transitive, it is said: "*wafartuhu afiruhu wafran wafirah*, so he is *mawfur* and *muwaffar*." Zuhayr said:

*"Whoever makes goodness at the expense of his honor will be made to lose it, and whoever does not guard against insult will be insulted."*

As for the intransitive, as in his saying: "*wafara* the wealth *yafiru wufuran*, so he is *wafir*." According to the first view, the meaning is "a recompense that is made full and complete." According to the second view, the meaning is "a recompense that is full and abundant." The word ﴿jaza'an﴾ is put in the accusative as a verbal noun (*masdar*).

If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few."﴾ ﴿He said, "Go! Whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense."﴾ In this passage there are several issues.

The first issue: concerning the manner of the coherence (*nazm*, the arrangement and connection of the verses), there are several aspects.

The first: Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in a great trial from his people and the people of his time, He explained that the condition of the prophets with the people of their times was similar. Do you not see that the first of the friends of Allah was Adam, and then he was in a severe trial from Iblis?

The second: the people only disputed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), opposed him, and proposed to him false suggestions, for two reasons: arrogance and envy. As for arrogance, their pride prevented them from submitting. As for envy, they envied him for what Allah had given him of prophethood and high rank. So He, exalted is He, explained that these two, arrogance and envy, are what led Iblis to leave faith and enter disbelief. Thus this is an ancient affliction and a great trial for creation.

The third: when He, exalted is He, described them by saying ﴿But it only increases them in great rebellion﴾ [al-Isra: 60], He explained what is the cause of the occurrence of this rebellion, namely the saying of Iblis, ﴿I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few.﴾ For the sake of this purpose, Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the story of Iblis and Adam. This is the discussion concerning the manner of the coherence.

The second issue: know that Allah, exalted is He, has mentioned this story in seven surahs: al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr, this surah, al-Kahf, Ta-Ha, and Sad. The complete discussion of it has already been given in al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, and al-Hijr, so there is no benefit in repetition, but there is no harm in enumerating some issues:

The first issue: they differed as to whether those commanded to prostrate to Adam were all the angels or specifically the angels of the earth. The apparent wording "the angels" indicates generality, but His saying, exalted is He, at the end of surah al-A'raf, describing the angels of the heavens, ﴿and to Him they prostrate﴾ [al-A'raf: 206], requires that the angels of the heavens be excluded from this generality.

The second issue: the prostration in this context may mean placing the forehead on the ground, or it may mean a greeting. On the first interpretation, was Adam the one prostrated to, or is it said that the one prostrated to was Allah, exalted is He, and Adam was a direction (*qiblah*) for the prostration?

The third issue: is Iblis among the angels or not? If he was not among the angels, how does the command to the angels to prostrate include him?

The fourth issue: was Iblis a disbeliever from the very beginning, or is it said that he only disbelieved at that time?

The fifth issue: did the angels prostrate to Adam from the moment his life was complete, or after that?

The sixth issue: is Iblis's argument for refusing to prostrate his saying ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾, or something else?

The seventh issue: these verses indicate that Iblis knew his Lord, but he fell into disbelief because of arrogance and envy. Some have denied this and said he never knew Allah at all.

The eighth issue: what is the wisdom behind Allah granting Iblis respite and giving him power over creation to whisper (*waswasah*)?

Let us return to the exegesis. We say: in this verse, He, exalted is He, related from Iblis one kind of action and two kinds of speech. As for the action, it is that he did not prostrate to Adam, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿they prostrated, except Iblis﴾. As for the two kinds of speech:

The first of them is his saying ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ This is an interrogative with the meaning of denial. Its meaning is that my origin is more noble than his origin, so it is necessary that I be more noble than him, and it is repugnant to reason that the more noble be commanded to serve the less noble.

The second kind of his speech is his saying ﴿Tell me, is this the one You have honored over me?﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: His saying ﴿Tell me (*ara'aytaka*)﴾ means "inform me." We have already investigated this expression in the commentary on surah al-An'am. His saying ﴿is this the one You have honored over me﴾ has several aspects:

The first: its meaning is "Inform me about this one whom You have preferred over me. Why did You prefer him over me, when I am better than him?" Then the speech was shortened because it is understood.

The second: it may be said that this is a subject with the interrogative particle omitted, and "the one" with its relative clause is the predicate. Its estimated form is "Inform me, is this the one whom You have honored over me!" This is in a manner of belittling and disparaging. The interrogative particle was omitted because its presence in His saying ﴿ara'aytaka﴾ made its repetition unnecessary.

The third aspect: this may be the object of "ara'ayta," because the *kaf* came merely for the address and has no grammatical position. It is as if he said, in a manner of wonder and denial, "Did you see or know this one whom you have honored over me?", meaning: if you had seen him or known him, you would have been obligated not to honor him over me. This is the real meaning of this expression. Then Allah, exalted is He, said, relating [from him], ﴿If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely take control of his descendants, except a few.﴾ Concerning this there are discussions:

The first discussion: Ibn Kathir read ﴿akhkhartani﴾ with the *ya'* (the final "ya" of the first person) retained both in pausing and in continuous recitation. 'Asim, Ibn 'Amir, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read it with the *ya'* omitted. Nafi' and Abu 'Amr retained it in continuous recitation but omitted it in pausing.

The second discussion: concerning *ihtinak* there are two views:

One of them: it is an expression for taking entirely. It is said: "Fulan *ihtanaka* what Fulan has of wealth," when he exhausted it and took it entirely. And "the locusts *ihtanaka* the crop" when they consumed it entirely.

The second: it comes from the Arab saying "*hannaka* the animal, *yuhannikuha*," when one places a rope under its lower jaw by which he leads it. Abu Muslim said: *ihtinak* is a form from *hanak* (the jaw/palate), as if they [the descendants] are controlled by him as the rider controls his horse by its bridle. According to the first view, the meaning of the verse is "I will certainly uproot them through misguidance." According to the second view, the meaning is "I will certainly lead them to sins as the animal is led by its rope."

The third discussion: His saying ﴿except a few﴾ refers to those whom Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾. If it is asked: how did Iblis form this true assumption concerning the descendants of Adam? We say: there are several aspects:

The first: he heard the angels saying ﴿Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], so he came to know these conditions.

The second: he whispered to Adam and did not find in him determination, so he assumed that his offspring would be like him in weakness of resolve.

The third: he knew that man is composed of a bestial appetitive power, a predatory irascible power, an imaginative satanic power, and a rational angelic power. He knew that the three powers, namely the appetitive, the irascible, and the imaginative, are the ones that dominate at the beginning of creation, and that the rational power is only perfected at the end. When the matter is like this, what Iblis said is necessarily true.

Know that when He, exalted is He, related this from Iblis, He related from Himself that He said to him, "Go." This "go" is not the going which is the opposite of coming; rather its meaning is "proceed to your affair which you have chosen," and the intent is to leave him free and to entrust the matter to him.

Then He said ﴿Whoever of them follows you, indeed Hell is your recompense, a full recompense.﴾ A parallel to this is the saying of Musa, peace be upon him, ﴿So go, for you will have in this life that you say, "No touching"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 97]. If it is asked: is it not better to say "indeed Hell is their recompense, a full recompense," so that this pronoun refers back to His saying ﴿whoever follows you﴾? We say there are several aspects:

The first: the estimated form is "indeed Hell is their recompense and your recompense," then the addressee was given precedence over the absent party, so it was said "your recompense."

The second: it is permissible that this address is directed to the absent parties by way of *iltifat* (the shift from one grammatical person to another).

The third: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: ("Whoever establishes an evil practice, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection.") So every act of disobedience that occurs results in Iblis acquiring a share equal to the burden of that doer. Since Iblis is the origin of all acts of disobedience, the one addressed with the threat is Iblis. Then He said ﴿a full recompense (*jaza'an mawfuran*)﴾. This word may be used transitively and intransitively. As for the transitive, it is said: "*wafartuhu afiruhu wafran wafirah*, so he is *mawfur* and *muwaffar*." Zuhayr said:

*"Whoever makes goodness at the expense of his honor will be made to lose it, and whoever does not guard against insult will be insulted."*

As for the intransitive, as in his saying: "*wafara* the wealth *yafiru wufuran*, so he is *wafir*." According to the first view, the meaning is "a recompense that is made full and complete." According to the second view, the meaning is "a recompense that is full and abundant." The word ﴿jaza'an﴾ is put in the accusative as a verbal noun (*masdar*).

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 17, verse 64:**

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and urge against them your horse and your foot, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs.﴾

Page 6

Know that when Iblis asked Allah for a respite until the Day of Resurrection, in order that he might seize (tahnik) the offspring of Adam, Allah the Exalted mentioned several things:

The first of them: His saying ﴿Go﴾, and its meaning: I have granted you respite for this period.

The second of them: His saying, the Exalted, ﴿and incite whomever you can among them﴾. It is said: afazzahu al-khawf and istafazzahu, meaning it disturbed him and made him light-headed (istakhaffahu). "Your voice" means his calling them to disobedience of Allah the Exalted. It has also been said: he meant by "your voice" singing, idle amusement and play. The form of the imperative here carries the sense of threat, as one says: "Strive your utmost, and you will see what will befall you."

The third of them: ﴿and urge against them your horse and your foot﴾. Regarding His saying ﴿and urge (wa ajlib)﴾ there are several views:

The first: al-Farra' said: it is from al-jalaba, which is shouting; they sometimes say al-jalab just as they say al-ghalaba and al-ghalab, and ash-shafaqa and ash-shafaq. Al-Layth and Abu 'Ubayda said: ajlabu and jalabu, from shouting.

The second: al-Zajjaj said, regarding fa'ala and af'ala: ajlaba 'ala al-'aduww ijlaban when he gathered horsemen against the enemy.

The third: Ibn al-Sikkit said: it is said, "they ajlibu against him," meaning they help against him.

The fourth: Tha'lab related from Ibn al-A'rabi: ajlaba ar-rajulu 'ala ar-rajuli when he threatened him with harm and gathered a host against him. So His saying "and urge against them" means, according to al-Farra': shout against them with your horse and your foot; according to al-Zajjaj: gather against them everything you are able to of your stratagems, and the ba' in "bi-khaylika" is then superfluous according to this view; and according to Ibn al-Sikkit it means: help against them with your horse and your foot, and the object of ijlab in this view is omitted, as if he seeks help in misleading them with his horse and his foot. This also comes close to the view of Ibn al-A'rabi.

They differed in the interpretation of "horse" (khayl) and "foot" (rajl). Abu adh-Dhuha related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Every rider or walker in disobedience of Allah the Exalted is of the horse of Iblis and his army." This includes every rider and walker in disobedience of Allah the Exalted. On this interpretation, his horse and his foot are everyone who joins him in calling to disobedience.

The second view: it is possible that Iblis has an army of devils, some of whom ride and some of whom walk.

The third view: that what is meant by it is the striking of a parable, as you say to a man who is diligent in a matter, "You have come to us with your horse and your foot." This view is closer. The word "khayl" applies to horsemen, and he, upon him be prayer and peace, said: "O horses of Allah, mount!" It may also apply to mares specifically. The intended meaning here is the first. "Rajl" is the plural of rajil, as they say tājir and tajr, sāhib and sahb, rākib and rakb. Hafs related from 'Asim: "wa rajilika" with a kasra on the jim, while others read it with a damma. Abu Zayd said: it is said rajul and rajil with the same meaning, and similarly ḥadut and ḥadith, nadus and nadis. Ibn al-Anbari said: Tha'lab informed us from al-Farra', who said: it is said rajul, rajil and rajlān with the same meaning.

The fourth of the things Allah the Exalted mentioned to Iblis is His saying: ﴿and share with them in wealth and children﴾. We say: as for sharing in wealth, it is an expression for every corrupt disposal of wealth, whether that corruption is due to taking it from other than its rightful source or placing it where it does not belong. It includes usury, usurpation, theft and corrupt transactions. Thus al-Qadi said, and it is a fine delimitation. As for the exegetes, they have mentioned several views. Qatada said: sharing in wealth is that they made the baḥīrah and the sā'ibah. 'Ikrimah said: it is an expression for their slitting the ears of cattle. It was also said: it is that they set aside a portion of their wealth for other than Allah the Exalted, as He said: ﴿So they say: "This is for Allah, by their claim, and this is for our partners"﴾ (al-An'am: 136). The most correct is what al-Qadi said.

As for sharing in children, they mentioned several views:

One of them: that it is calling to fornication. Al-Asamm rejected this, saying that there is no blame upon the child. It may be answered that what is meant is: share with them in the means of acquiring children, and that is by calling to fornication.

The second: that they name their children 'Abd al-Lat and 'Abd al-'Uzza.

The third: that they make their children desire false religions, such as Judaism, Christianity and others.

The fourth: their hastening to kill children and bury them alive.

The fifth: their encouraging them to memorize poetry containing obscenity, and encouraging them toward killing, fighting, and vile and wicked crafts. The principle is to say that every conduct by a person toward his child in a way that leads to committing an evil or

Page 7

ugly deed is included in it.

**The fifth category** of the things Allah the Exalted mentioned concerning Iblis in this verse is His saying: ﴿And promise them﴾.

Know that since the aim of Satan is to encourage false belief and false action, and to deter from true belief and true action, and since it is known that encouraging something is only possible by establishing that there is absolutely no harm in doing it while it still yields great benefits, and deterring from something is only possible by establishing that there is no benefit in doing it while it still brings great harms, then, once this is established, we say: when Satan calls to disobedience, he must first establish that there is no harm whatsoever in the act. This can only be done if he says: there is no resurrection, no Paradise, no Fire, and no life after this life. By this method he establishes in the person's mind that there is absolutely no harm in committing these sins. And when he has finished with this stage, he establishes in the person's mind that this act yields various kinds of pleasure and joy, and that human life in this world is only possible through it, so that forgoing it is a loss and a deprivation, as the poet said:

*Take your share of joy and pleasure,*
*For every one of them, however long the span, passes away.*

This is the method of calling to disobedience. As for the method of deterring from obedience, it is that he first establishes in the person's mind that there is no benefit in it. This is established in two ways:

The first: he says there is no Paradise, no Fire, no reward, and no punishment.

The second: these acts of worship have no benefit for the worshipper or the One worshipped, so they are pure futility. By these two methods Satan establishes in the person's mind that there is no benefit in them. And when he has finished with this stage, he says that they entail hardship and tribulation, and that is the greatest of harms. These are the comprehensive forms of Satan's deception. So His saying ﴿And promise them﴾ encompasses all these categories. The commentators said: ﴿And promise them﴾, that is, by saying there is no Paradise and no Fire. Others said: ﴿And promise them﴾ by postponing repentance. Others said: ﴿And promise them﴾ with false hopes, like his saying to Adam: ﴿Your Lord has only forbidden you this tree lest you become angels or become of the immortal﴾ (al-A'raf: 20). Others said: promise them the intercession of idols with Allah the Exalted, and noble lineages, and preferring the immediate over the deferred. In sum, these categories are many, and all of them fall within the principle we have mentioned. If you wish to investigate this subject further, consult the book *Dhamm al-Ghurur* from *Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din* by Shaykh al-Ghazali, until your intellect comprehends the comprehensive aspects of Iblis's deception.

Know that when Allah the Exalted said ﴿And promise them﴾, He followed it with what would serve as a deterrent from accepting his promise, saying: ﴿Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾. The reason for this is that he only calls to one of three matters: satisfying desire, carrying out anger, and seeking leadership and high rank. He never calls at all to knowing Allah the Exalted or to serving Him. These three matters are illusory in many respects:

First: in reality they are not pleasures but rather a release from pains.

Second: even if they are pleasures, they are base pleasures shared with dogs, worms, beetles, and others.

Third: they are quick to pass away, to end, and to perish.

Fourth: they are only attained with many hardships and great toils.

Fifth: the pleasures of the belly and the genitals are only completed by handling foul, rotten, repugnant moistures.

Sixth: they are not lasting, but are followed by death, decrepitude, poverty, regret over what has been lost, and fear of death. Since these objectives, although apparently delightful, are mixed with these great calamities and grave transgressions, encouraging them is deception. For this very reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Satan promises them nothing but delusion﴾.

Know that when Allah said to Iblis, "Do what you can," He said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them.﴾ Concerning this there are two opinions:

[Page 8]

The first: the intended meaning is all of Allah's servants who are obligated (to follow the law). This is the view of Abu 'Ali al-Jubba'i, who said: The evidence for this is that Allah the Exalted made an exception from it in many verses, for those who follow him, by His saying: ﴿except those who follow you﴾ (al-Hijr: 42). He then used this to argue that Iblis and his armies have no means of throwing people down or confusing their intellects, and that his power extends only as far as whispering. He reinforced this with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me, so do not blame me but blame yourselves﴾ (Ibrahim: 22). Furthermore, if he had the power to do these deeds, he would have to confuse the people of virtue and knowledge rather than the rest of the people, so that his harm would be greater. Then he said: His intellect is lost not due to Satan but due to the predominance of corrupt humours; and it is not impossible that one of the causes of that illness is the belief that Satan is approaching him, so fear overcomes him and that illness arises.

The second opinion: the intended meaning of His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants﴾ is the people of virtue, knowledge, and faith, because of what we explained earlier, that the word "servants" in the Qur'an is specific to the people of faith. The evidence for this is that He said in another verse: ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally﴾ (al-Nahl: 100).

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾. Concerning this there are two discussions:

The first discussion: when Allah enabled Iblis to bring about the utmost of what he is able to do in the matter of whispering, and this became a cause for intense fear in the human heart, He said: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾. Its meaning is that although Satan is capable, Allah the Exalted is more capable than him, and more merciful to His servants than all. So He repels Satan's plotting from them and protects them from his misguidance and seduction.

The second discussion: this verse indicates that the one protected is only the one whom Allah the Exalted protects, and that a person cannot by himself guard against the places of error. For if advancing toward truth and refraining from falsehood came to a person from himself, it would have been necessary to say: "The person is sufficient for himself in guarding against Satan." Since He did not say that, but said ﴿And sufficient is your Lord﴾, we know that everything comes from Allah. For this reason the verifying scholars said: There is no power to avoid disobedience of Allah except by Allah's protection, and no strength to obey Allah except by Allah's enabling.

There remain two questions concerning the verse:

The first question: Did Iblis know that the One who spoke with him, saying ﴿and incite whom you can among them﴾, was the God of the worlds, or did he not know that? If he knew it, then since He said ﴿Indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense﴾, how did this severe threat not prevent him from disobedience, given that he heard it directly from Allah the Exalted without intermediary? And if he did not know that this speaker was the God of the worlds, how did he say ﴿Tell me, this one whom You have honored over me﴾?

The answer: perhaps he was uncertain about everything, or he was saying in every case whatever occurred to his mind by way of conjecture.

The second question: what is the wisdom in Allah the Exalted granting him respite until the Day of Resurrection and enabling him to whisper? A wise one, when he wills a matter and knows that something prevents its occurrence, does not strive to bring about that obstacle?

The answer: As for our school, the matter is clear in this regard. As for the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist theological school), they have two positions. Al-Jubba'i said: Allah the Exalted knew that those who disbelieved, upon Iblis's whispering, would disbelieve even supposing Iblis did not exist, and given that, his existence adds no further corruption. Abu Hashim said: it is not far-fetched that his existence produces further corruption, but Allah the Exalted kept him in existence to intensify the obligation upon creation, so that by means of that intensification they would deserve greater reward. We have mentioned these two views in the commentary on Surat al-A'raf and al-Hijr, and we went to great lengths in clarifying them. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 17, verses 66–69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away. And man is ever ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind (hasib) and then you will find for yourselves no protector?﴾ ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a storm of wind and drown you for your disbelief, and then you will find for yourselves against Us no pursuer?﴾

Know that He, may He be exalted, returned to mentioning the proofs that indicate His power, wisdom and mercy. We have already mentioned that the greatest aim of this noble Book is to establish the proofs of tawhid (the oneness of God). So whenever the discourse extends over one section, after it the discourse returns to mentioning the proofs of tawhid. What is mentioned here are the aspects derived from the blessings concerning the circumstances of riding the sea.

The first type: the manner of the ship's movement upon the surface of the sea, which is His saying: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea.﴾ Al-izja' (driving) is to propel a thing gradually, step by step, and we have mentioned this in the commentary on His saying: ﴿with goods of little value﴾ [Yusuf: 88]. The meaning is: Your Lord is He who causes the ship to move over the surface of the sea, ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, in pursuit of trade, ﴿indeed He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ The address in His saying ﴿Your Lord﴾ and in His saying ﴿Indeed He is ever Merciful to you﴾ is general with respect to everyone, and what is meant by mercy is the benefits and welfare of this world.

The second type: His saying: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea.﴾ By harm is meant severe fear, such as the fear of drowning. ﴿Those you call upon vanish except Him.﴾ The meaning is that in that state a person does not humble himself before an idol, the sun, the moon, an angel, or a ship, but humbles himself only before God, may He be exalted. ﴿But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away﴾ from faith and sincerity, after He has saved you from drowning and the sea and brought you out onto the land. ﴿And man is ever ungrateful﴾ for the blessings of God, because in hardship he clings to His bounty and mercy, but in ease and comfort he turns away from Him and clings to others.

The third type: His saying: ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will cause the side of the land to swallow you﴾. Al-Layth said: al-khasf and al-khusuf is the entering of one thing into another. It is said: "a sunken eye" (khasifa), which is one whose pupil has disappeared into the head; and "a sunken spring" (khasifa), meaning its water has receded; and "the sun was eclipsed" (khasafat), meaning it was concealed, as if it had fallen beneath a veil or entered a hole. So His saying ﴿that He cause the side of the land to swallow you﴾ means that He causes you to disappear into the side of the land, which is the earth. He said ﴿the side of the land﴾ because He mentioned the sea in the first verse, so the sea is a side and the land is a side. God, may He be exalted, informed that just as He is able to make them disappear into the water, He is also able to make them disappear into the earth. Drowning is a disappearance beneath the water, just as being swallowed up is a disappearance beneath the dust.

The sense of the discourse is this: In the first verse He mentioned that they were frightened of the terror of the sea, and when He delivered them from it, they believed. So He says: Suppose you were saved from the terror of the sea, how then do you feel secure from the terror of the land? He, may He be exalted, is able to send upon you the calamities of the land from below or from above. As for from below, it is by swallowing. As for from above, it is by raining stones upon them, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿or send against you a violent wind﴾. Just as they do not humble themselves except before God, may He be exalted, when riding the sea, so too they must not humble themselves except before Him in all circumstances.

The linguistic meaning of al-haṣb is throwing: it is said "I pelt (haṣabtu uhsibu haṣban) when you throw," and al-haṣab is the thing thrown. From it comes His saying: ﴿the fuel of Hell﴾, meaning they will be cast into it. The meaning of His saying ﴿hasiban﴾ is a punishment that pelts them, that is, throws stones at them. The wind that carries dust and pebbles is called hasib, and the cloud that throws down snow and hail is called hasib because it throws them down by pelting. Al-Zajjaj said: al-hasib is dust that contains pebbles, and according to this, al-hasib is "one possessing pebbles," like "one with milk" (laban) and "one with dates" (tamr). His saying ﴿then you will find for yourselves no protector﴾ means you will not find a helper who will help you and protect you from the punishment of God.

Then He said: ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will return you to it﴾, that is, to the sea, ﴿another time﴾. His saying ﴿and send against you a storm of wind﴾: al-qasif is the breaker. It is said: "he broke the thing (qasafa al-shay') breaking it (yaqsifuhu qasfan)" when he broke it violently. Al-qasif from the wind is the wind that breaks trees. Here He intends a severe wind that breaks the ship and drowns them. His saying ﴿and drown you for your disbelief﴾ means because of your disbelief. ﴿Then you will find for yourselves against Us no pursuer for it.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: that is, you will not find anyone who will pursue Us with a denial of what has befallen you, by turning it away from you. Do you not see that He said: ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that you should not take besides Me a guardian (wakil)﴾ [al-Isra': 2], shifting from the plural to the singular? Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 17, verses 66–69:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea, that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those you call upon vanish except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away. And man is ever ungrateful.﴾ ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind (hasib) and then you will find for yourselves no protector?﴾ ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a storm of wind and drown you for your disbelief, and then you will find for yourselves against Us no pursuer?﴾

Know that He, may He be exalted, returned to mentioning the proofs that indicate His power, wisdom and mercy. We have already mentioned that the greatest aim of this noble Book is to establish the proofs of tawhid (the oneness of God). So whenever the discourse extends over one section, after it the discourse returns to mentioning the proofs of tawhid. What is mentioned here are the aspects derived from the blessings concerning the circumstances of riding the sea.

The first type: the manner of the ship's movement upon the surface of the sea, which is His saying: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea.﴾ Al-izja' (driving) is to propel a thing gradually, step by step, and we have mentioned this in the commentary on His saying: ﴿with goods of little value﴾ [Yusuf: 88]. The meaning is: Your Lord is He who causes the ship to move over the surface of the sea, ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, in pursuit of trade, ﴿indeed He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ The address in His saying ﴿Your Lord﴾ and in His saying ﴿Indeed He is ever Merciful to you﴾ is general with respect to everyone, and what is meant by mercy is the benefits and welfare of this world.

The second type: His saying: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea.﴾ By harm is meant severe fear, such as the fear of drowning. ﴿Those you call upon vanish except Him.﴾ The meaning is that in that state a person does not humble himself before an idol, the sun, the moon, an angel, or a ship, but humbles himself only before God, may He be exalted. ﴿But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away﴾ from faith and sincerity, after He has saved you from drowning and the sea and brought you out onto the land. ﴿And man is ever ungrateful﴾ for the blessings of God, because in hardship he clings to His bounty and mercy, but in ease and comfort he turns away from Him and clings to others.

The third type: His saying: ﴿Do you then feel secure that He will cause the side of the land to swallow you﴾. Al-Layth said: al-khasf and al-khusuf is the entering of one thing into another. It is said: "a sunken eye" (khasifa), which is one whose pupil has disappeared into the head; and "a sunken spring" (khasifa), meaning its water has receded; and "the sun was eclipsed" (khasafat), meaning it was concealed, as if it had fallen beneath a veil or entered a hole. God, may He be exalted, informed that just as He is able to make them disappear into the water, He is also able to make them disappear into the earth. Drowning is a disappearance beneath the water, just as being swallowed up is a disappearance beneath the dust.

The sense of the discourse is this: In the first verse He mentioned that they were frightened of the terror of the sea, and when He delivered them from it, they believed. So He says: Suppose you were saved from the terror of the sea, how then do you feel secure from the terror of the land? He, may He be exalted, is able to send upon you the calamities of the land from below or from above. As for from below, it is by swallowing. As for from above, it is by raining stones upon them, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿or send against you a violent wind﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: al-hasib is dust that contains pebbles, and according to this, al-hasib is "one possessing pebbles," like "one with milk" (laban) and "one with dates" (tamr).
